title: Dispatch TUR 4: Warnings Name a Disaster on the Last Westmere Train
summary: A future account describes a crash at a bridge that does not exist.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Post Office yesterday released a letter addressed to the Westmere Railway’s safety inspector, an office abolished in 1883. Written by a guard named Amos Pell and dated 17 October 2038, it describes the evacuation train slowing at the marsh bridge shortly before midnight. The eastern span, Pell writes, will fail under its weight.

A further page, separated from the envelope when it reached the sorting room, lists 106 passengers and says only that the guard has “no second road home.” The list includes Miriam Harrow, aged eleven, and Theo Wren, aged ten. Mr. Wren has never had a grandson named Theo. His son and daughter-in-law expect their first child next spring.

No marsh bridge was built beyond the surviving pier. Dr. Saye maintains that the correspondence comes from a course the railway might still take through the Stratum, where an unrealized structure can have weight and consequence. She will not say whether the letters describe an inevitable future.

Mrs. Harrow now believes the letters were written by a child who knows her. She showed this newspaper a small drawing enclosed with the latest one: three red platform lamps and a woman holding a yellow umbrella. Mrs. Harrow owns the umbrella but says she has never brought it to the goods depot.

Mr. Pike has ordered postal staff to sort all Westmere mail by hand. He says one envelope remains unopened. It bears the cancellation time 11:58 p.m., two minutes after the bridge is said to fail, and is addressed simply to “Whoever Is Waiting at Alderwick.”
